chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Said from Ibn Abi Umayr from Jamil ibn Darradj from Muhammad ibn Muslim from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
He said to me: 'If you do not catch the congregation before the Imam says the Takbir for the bowing, then do not join them in that bowing.'
And from him (Al-Husayn ibn Said) from Safwan from Al-As'ad from Muhammad ibn Muslim from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
'Do not count as a valid bowing the one in which you did not witness its Takbir with the Imam.'
And from him (Al-Husayn ibn Said) from Al-Nadr from Asim from Muhammad ibn Muslim from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
'When you catch the Takbir before the Imam bows, you have caught the prayer.'
As for what was narrated - Al-Husayn ibn Said from Al-Nadr from Hisham ibn Salim from Sulayman ibn Khalid from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)
He said: 'Regarding a man who catches the Imam while he is bowing; the man says Takbir while keeping his back straight, then bows before the Imam raises his head; he has caught the bowing.'
And what was narrated - Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Ibn Abi Umayr from Hammad from Al-Halabi from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

He said: 'When you catch the Imam and he has already bowed, and you say Takbir and bow before he raises his head, you have caught the bowing; and if the Imam raises his head before you bow, you have missed the bowing.'

So these two reports do not contradict what we presented earlier, because his saying (peace be upon him) in the first report 'when you catch the Imam while he is bowing' and in the second report 'and he has bowed' are attributed to joining him in the row, from which it is not permissible to delay in prayer if possible, even if one had caught the Takbir of bowing before that place. For whoever hears the Imam when he has said the Takbir of bowing, and there is a distance between him and the Imam, it is permissible for him to say Takbir and bow with him wherever the distance ends, then he may walk while bowing if he wishes until he joins him, or he may prostrate in his prayer. When he finishes from his two prostrations, he joins him, whichever of those he does. And when we attribute these two reports to this meaning, the reports do not contradict each other. And that which indicates the permissibility of what we mentioned is what was narrated:
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on joining congregational prayer if the Imam is already bowing?
ai.summary: In Shia jurisprudence, this narration from the Imams (specifically Abu Ja'far and Abu Abdillah) clarifies the precise moment of 'catching up' (idrak) in congregational prayer, emphasizing that the Takbir must be heard while the worshipper is still standing to validly count the subsequent Ruku'. The text resolves apparent contradictions between narrations by distinguishing between catching the Takbir at one's current spot versus joining the Imam's row, a nuance critical for determining the validity of individual rak'ahs. This reflects the Shia scholarly tradition's rigorous attention to the physical and auditory conditions of following the Imam.
